sections.title: Sound of S
paragraphs: You call this letter (S) /es/. It mostly sounds like (sun) /sʌn/, which means the bright star in our day sky. This letter makes four different sounds in English words.

sections.title: How to say S
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your tongue tip near the bump behind your top teeth. Push air through the small gap without your voice. For the second sound, make that exact same air stream and turn your voice on. Feel your throat buzz. For the third sound, pull your tongue slightly back and round your lips while your voice hums. For the fourth sound, keep that same mouth shape and turn your voice off.

sections.title: Spelling of S
paragraphs: At the start of words or before quiet sounds, the letter makes the sound /s/, as in (stop) /stɒp/. Between vowels or after loud voiced sounds, it sounds like /z/, as in (rose) /roʊz/. When it sits before the endings ion or ual after a vowel, it makes the sound /ʒ/, like in (vision) /vɪ.ʒən/. Before ure or in special common words, it sounds like /ʃ/, as in (sugar) /ʃʊɡ.ər/.

sections.title: Mistakes with S
paragraphs: Learners often make a quiet hissing sound when the letter should buzz like a bee. Do not say the sound /s/ when the letter sits between two vowels. Make sure your vocal cords vibrate, just like the sound in the word zoo. Another common error is adding an extra vowel sound right before the letter at the start of a word. Start cleanly with pure air.
